PullRequest.Title: sessions: enable archive nudge by default
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Enable `chat.agentSessions.archiveNudge.enabled` by default on Stable starting with VS Code 1.142. Existing explicit user settings and experiment assignments continue to take precedence.

The preceding Stable experiment increased archive participation by 4.66% relative over its planned 14-day window. Request participation decreased by 0.82% relative and crossed the prespecified guardrail; the owner explicitly accepted that tradeoff for rollout. Stable 1.138-1.141 clients are covered separately by a bounded ExP treatment rollout.

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9415

## Validation

- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/chat.contribution.ts` — passed (using the existing dependency installation from the primary checkout)
- Unit tests not run; this is a one-line configuration-default change and existing explicit override behavior is unchanged.

## Test plan

1. Launch a Stable build without an explicit `chat.agentSessions.archiveNudge.enabled` setting and verify the registered default is `true`.
2. Set the setting to `false` and verify the explicit override remains effective.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed Stable default, enabled/disabled lifecycle branches, retained-poller test assertions, 60-second scheduler, and two concrete REST calls per refresh are all directly traced. Only how long users leave such a view visible and typical PR count are uncertain, which affects magnitude rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Authenticated GitHub HTTP requests, response processing, and retained PR model/polling objects.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows as 2 * distinct associated PRs * visible minutes, with additional review-page requests possible when the reviews endpoint returns changed paginated data. Polling is coalesced per shared PR model but is not bounded by nudge age.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Persistent excessive network I/O and GitHub API quota consumption while an already-actionable archive nudge remains on screen.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: On Stable the default was false. The nudge temporarily resolved/polled candidate PRs only until reportWouldShow cleared experimentTriggerPending; eligibleSession then became undefined and its derived-store references and polling handles were disposed. The disabled-path test confirms references=0 and polling=0 after that transition.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Defaulting the setting to true keeps eligibleSession alive after reportWouldShow and after every PR reaches Merged, so the models derived at sessionArchiveNudge.ts:375-383 retain one startPolling handle per distinct PR for as long as the completed session remains visible and the nudge is not dismissed, archived, or superseded.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `default: true` at chat.contribution.ts:562 changes Stable users without an override from the disposing disabled branch to the enabled branch. sessionArchiveNudge.test.ts:438-449 explicitly verifies that an enabled, already-merged two-PR nudge retains `references: 2, polling: 2`, whereas the disabled test at lines 318-331 ends with `polling: 0`.
Findings.Title: Stop polling terminal PRs when enabling the nudge
Findings.Impact: A Stable user who leaves a completed merged session visible now generates about 120 authenticated GitHub requests per distinct PR per hour despite merged being terminal. Multi-PR sessions multiply this traffic, consuming rate-limit budget and network/CPU resources and potentially throttling user-initiated GitHub operations.
Findings.Evidence: Each retained GitHubPullRequestModel polls every 60 seconds (githubPullRequestModel.ts:14,103-129). Every refresh performs getPullRequest and getReviews concurrently (lines 134-137), which issue authenticated REST requests to `/pulls/{n}` and `/reviews` (githubPRFetcher.ts:194-220) with the renderer cache disabled (githubApiClient.ts:150-164). Model references are shared per PR, so effective fan-out is one poller and at least two HTTP requests per distinct associated PR per minute; the nudge does not add duplicate polling for a PR already polled by another consumer.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain the resolved model state needed to render the nudge, but dispose or avoid each polling handle once its PR is Merged (or at least stop all polling once every candidate is merged); restart only when the candidate PR set changes.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stable startup and workbench restoration with no session chat visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configuration registration occurs during module setup; the eager nudge service and AfterRestored contribution already existed and their catalogue/storage autorun does not read the changed enablement value. No new work is added to the startup critical path by the default itself.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of restored sessions scanned by the pre-existing service autorun; unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous pre-existing catalogue/profile-storage scan; no changed queue, limiter, or asynchronous fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Profile dismissal/impression values are read as before; changing the registered default does not alter their keys, lifetime, or invalidation when no view creates a SessionArchiveNudge.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the service constructor and contribution lifecycle were inspected, and enablement is only consumed by the per-view SessionArchiveNudge.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session-catalogue size varies, but its scan is identical before and after the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No startup performance regression; the changed default only affects the per-view enabled branch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a visible completed agent session whose distinct GitHub PRs are not yet all merged
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The chat view can render and remain interactive without these requests; only nudge eligibility waits for each PR model to obtain authoritative state. The initial refresh and polling are therefore on the nudge-display path, not the main view-render critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticated GitHub REST GET for pull-request metadata and reviews
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: An initial pair of requests per distinct PR, then at least two requests per PR per minute while eligibility remains active; changed reviews can require additional pages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old Stable default still performed this work temporarily while the one-window experiment trigger was pending, but after that trigger a default-disabled window skipped future eligible sessions. The new default keeps this path active for every qualifying Stable session without an override.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only before the archive nudge can determine that every PR is merged; off the main chat-view rendering critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct valid GitHub PRs after artifact/association deduplication and enterprise-host exclusion; realistic sessions commonly have one or a few PRs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One shared model and poll scheduler per distinct PR. Each model launches pull-request and reviews requests concurrently, so a cycle can issue 2N concurrent requests; per-model refresh promises coalesce overlaps and references share models, but there is no aggregate limiter across different PR keys.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Models are reference-counted and shared by normalized PR key. ETags permit 304 responses, but the request service cache is explicitly disabled, so warm cycles still cross the network. Failed refreshes are not negatively cached and retry on the next 60-second poll.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: eligibility, normalized deduplication, reference sharing, refresh coalescing, REST endpoints, and scheduler interval were directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical PR count and how often users inspect completed sessions vary; model sharing can eliminate incremental requests when the same PR already has an active polling consumer.
Scenarios.Verdict: The initial authoritative read is necessary for the enabled feature and realistic cardinality is small, so it is not a separate finding; the reportable issue is the unnecessary continuation after all states are terminal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Leave an already-merged archive nudge visible in a completed session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After all PRs are Merged the nudge is already rendered, so subsequent polling is entirely off the critical path and cannot change the terminal eligibility result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Repeated GitHub pull-request and reviews REST polling after all PRs are merged
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least 2N HTTP requests per minute, approximately 120N per hour, for the visible lifetime of the nudge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With the old Stable false default, reportWouldShow cleared experimentTriggerPending and eligibleSession became undefined, releasing references and poll handles; tests confirm polling=0. The true default keeps them live, and enabled-path tests confirm polling=N even for already-merged PRs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No critical-path benefit after merged state is established; it consumes background network and GitHub rate-limit budget.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct associated PRs multiplied by the number of minutes the completed session remains visible before dismissal, continuation, archive, or view hiding.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One poll scheduler per shared PR model; schedulers created together tend to produce bursts of 2N concurrent REST requests every 60 seconds. Sharing prevents duplicate schedulers for the same key, but there is no cross-key limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ETags reduce response bodies on warm polls, but every cycle still authenticates and performs HTTP because transport caching is disabled. Polling has no age bound and remains live with the nudge.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: enabled/disabled test assertions, observable ownership, 60-second scheduling, and two concrete REST calls per refresh directly prove the lifetime and cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The duration users leave a completed session visible and N determine total traffic; exact prevalence is unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium network regression: the default rollout materially amplifies unbounded terminal-state polling. A finding was submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dismiss, continue, hide, or archive from the nudge
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hiding the view, sending a post-impression turn, dismissing, or archiving invalidates eligibility and disposes model references/poll handles. Archive activation optionally waits for one onboarding presentation, then awaits the provider archive operation before reporting completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider-specific session archive, which may update a local agent model or cross the remote-agent/provider boundary
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one provider archive call per user activation; no active-chat cancellation is expected under nudge eligibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The action was available only to explicitly enabled/experiment-assigned Stable users; the default exposes the same one-shot operation broadly without changing its implementation or cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Intentionally awaited because it is the requested archive action; it is user initiated rather than background work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One current session and its associated PR model set; archive cancellation loops scale with active chats, but nudge eligibility requires the session and peer chats to be inactive, so this path normally has zero cancellations and one provider archive call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cleanup is reactive and disposes all per-PR handles together. On archive, onboarding and provider archive are serialized; no diff-introduced burst or repeated invocation occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Dismissal/impression/profile keys are persisted and invalidated on archive/delete/unarchive as before. Once an impression records continuation, the exposed PR set is suppressed; there is no repeated model creation for that set.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cardinality and sequencing; provider-specific boundary cost varies by session backend.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider implementations vary in remote and filesystem cost, but invocation remains a single explicit user action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding: cleanup correctly bounds polling, and the one-shot archive boundary is intentional and serialized.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed hunk and its per-view, GitHub-model, request, rendering, storage, and archive call paths. Submitted one medium finding for retained per-PR GitHub polling after terminal merged state; no startup, rendering, cache, concurrency, or user-triggered archive regression independently met the reporting threshold.
